Adventure bottom movement HUD: native text and branch reconstruction

This is original-image source material, not an executed display or a test.
The configured Steam/reference and official/classic PE identities, paths,
SHA-256 values and function boundaries are retained in pe-functions.tsv.
The complete renderer is retained as ASM, branch/condition/call/operand TSV,
and separately as the actual Ghidra C decompilation. The focused HUD slice
is pe-{edition}-movement-hud.asm. This is a different owner from the movement
modal at reference RVA 0x874800.

Address convention
  renderer reference 0xAF1190..0xB0390E (code; unwind ends at 0xB03C40)
           classic   0xAEE1D0..0xB0094E (code; unwind ends at 0xB00C80)
  HUD reference 0xAFA863..0xAFB3DF; classic subtracts 0x2FC0.
  swimming predicate reference 0x7E0610..0x7E069B;
                     classic   0x7DDE90..0x7DDF1B.
  effective speed reference 0x1334C10..0x13356BA;
                  classic   0x132FB80..0x133062A.
  The predicate and speed supplier have multiple chained .pdata chunks;
  retaining only their first unwind records would omit real return paths.

HUD eligibility and effective actor (0xAFA863..0xAFA941)
  actor = global adventure player, reference global RVA 0x23E5110.
  No box if actor is null, or renderer's player+0x110 bit0x2 flag is set.
  If actor+0x110 bit0x200 is set, look up actor+0x3DC using unit lookup
  reference 0x73B70 / classic 0x73B00. Use the returned mount when non-null;
  otherwise retain actor. All gait/speed fields below use this effective actor.

  if int16(actor+0x4CC) != -30000 or int32(actor+0x4D4) != -1:
      category = 4
  elif actor+0x114 bit0x1 or actor+0x118 bit0x40000:
      category = 2
  elif actor+0x110 bit0x8000:
      category = 3
  elif swimming_gait_predicate(actor):
      category = 1
  else:
      category = 0

  selected = int32(actor+0xDE8 + 4*category)
  vector = actor.raw_at_0x5F8.gaits_at_0xE8 + 0x18*category
  No box when selected < 0 or selected >= vector.size().
  A bad name index does not suppress the box; it selects the Move fallback.

  swimming_gait_predicate(actor):
      require int32(actor+0x1280) > 2
      require byte(*(actor+0x1278)+2) bit0x8
      require int16(actor+0xC42) > (int16(actor+0xC40) >> 1)
              or int16(actor+0xC40) == 0
      require int16(actor+0x800) <= 0
      require int16(actor+0x804) < 10
      require int32(actor+0x978) < 100
      return true; any failed requirement returns false
  Native synchronization helper 0x1385B10 is retained at its original calls.

Every title source (0xAFA94E..0xAFA9CC)
  if int16(actor+0x4CC) != -30000:
      title = "Climb"                 # reference literal RVA 0x167D254
  else:
      gait = vector[selected]
      nameIndex = int32(gait+0)
      if nameIndex >= 0 and nameIndex < world.gait_names.size():
          title = world.gait_names[nameIndex]
      else:
          title = "Move"              # reference literal RVA 0x16AE908
  reference gait-name vector RVA 0x24ECAB8; classic RVA 0x24E69A8.
  classic literal RVAs are Climb 0x167798C and Move 0x16A9B88.

  The names are dynamic GAIT raw data, not a native Walk/Run/Sprint switch.
  All 37 vanilla names and their creature/caste/variation provenance are in
  ../adventure-movement/raw-gait-sources.tsv and raw-gait-applications.tsv.
  The scope Adventure movement already supplies all 37 names plus Climb/Move.
  Mod-provided names can add arbitrary strings through the same native vector.

Native long-name branch (0xAFA9CC..0xAFAA2E)
  if title.length() >= 20:
      title.resize(19)
      title[16] = title[17] = title[18] = '.'
  The only vanilla name reaching this branch is Maximum Flight Speed, which
  becomes "Maximum Flight S..." before the name draw.
  The original complete string is available before native resize. Translating
  the truncated spelling alone loses the full-name source and misses this case.

  Native title draw call reference RVA 0xAFAB92, return 0xAFAB97;
                         classic   RVA 0xAF7BD2, return 0xAF7BD7.
  This field is the screenshot's cyan name above the green speed.
  Its native draw is separate from every number and direction glyph below.
  Title color uses actor+0x110 bit0x40000; it adds no new wording.

All numeric productions
  speed(unit, current) is the native effective-speed supplier, called with
  second argument 0 and current in the third argument. Preserve its result.
  value(unit,current) = signed_trunc(1000000 / (speed(unit,current) + 100)).
  No branch below contains additional English text. Punctuation is '.', '/'
  and decimal digit/zero-padding strings.

  1. Climbing target exists (0xAFAB97..0xAFAECC):
     If int16(actor+0x4CC) != -30000:
         draw full_decimal(value(actor, true)) at call 0xAFAD3C.
     Color uses fatigue actor+0x984 (<2000, 2000..3999, >=4000).

  2. Normal speed differs from the current speed (0xAFAED1..0xAFB179):
     v0 = value(actor, false); v1 = value(actor, true).
     If v0 != v1:
         draw ratio_component(v1) + "/" + ratio_component(v0)
         at call 0xAFB162.
     This is the screenshot's 1.8/4.0 production.

  3. Normal and current speed are equal (0xAFB179..0xAFB305):
     If v0 == v1:
         draw full_decimal(v1) at call 0xAFB2DE.

  full_decimal(value):
      q = signed_trunc(value / 1000)
      result = decimal(q) + "."
      remainder = decimal(value - q*1000)
      if remainder.length <= 2: result += "0"
      if remainder.length == 1: result += "0"
      result += remainder
      Native code then trims the temporary remainder when length >= 4 and
      its last two characters are zero. The remainder was already appended
      by value; that cleanup does not trim the rendered result.

  ratio_component(value):
      q = signed_trunc(value / 1000)
      result = decimal(q)
      if result.length == 1:
          result += "." + decimal(signed_trunc((value-q*1000) / 100))
      return result

Every direction glyph branch
  Climbing builds bits by comparing target int16 +0x4CC/+0x4CE/+0x4D0
  with position +0xA8/+0xAA/+0xAC. Normal movement uses byte actor+0x4C4.
  Direction bits: y< 1, y> 2, x> 4, x< 8, z> 0x10, z< 0x20.
  Dispatch input is (bits & 15)-1; inputs outside 0..9 emit no planar glyph.
  Reference dispatch/table pairs:
      climb  0xAFAE37 / 0xB03B18 (default 0xAFAE62)
      normal 0xAFB342 / 0xB03B40 (default 0xAFB36D)
  Both have every selector alias retained in pe-switches.tsv and are supplied
  to Ghidra as JumpTable overrides, including selectors that emit no glyph.

      bits & 15 = 1: '^'; 2: 'v'; 3: none; 4: '>'; 5: tile byte 0xBF;
                  6: tile byte 0xD9; 7: none; 8: '<'; 9: tile byte 0xDA;
                  10: tile byte 0xC0; 0 or 11..15: none.
  Independent bit0x10 emits tile byte0x18; independent bit0x20 emits byte0x19.
  These remain native glyph draws and are not additional words for translation.

Native raw speed processing, including its numeric and state branches, remains
in the complete effective-movement-speed source and Ghidra C. The translation
only needs the title production; numeric, fatigue-color and direction paths
remain native and preserve all their original branch results.
